title: Edmonton family settles over fatal cop chase
article: An Edmonton woman who lost a son in a horrific crash with an Edmonton police cruiser in June 2001 said Wednesday her family just wants to move on, after agreeing to an out-of-court settlement.

Gloria Ramirez said she cannot reveal details of the settlement for the fiery collision with the unmarked police vehicle. The family had named the city, the police service, the officers involved, Ford Motor Corp. and others in the suit.

Gloria, her father Carlos, and her two sons - Giovanni Aleman, 7, and Jonathan Aleman, 6,- were in their Ford Tempo when it was struck at an intersection by Const. Ken Brander, who was driving at speeds of up to 120 km/h. Giovanni died four days later, and Jonathan was left with burns so severe he lost both his hands.
"No matter, you know, that the settlement was done ... it'll never bring back Giovanni and it'll never bring back Jonathan's life ... the way it was before," she said.

In September 2003, a judge acquitted Brander of criminal negligence causing death, and three counts of criminal negligence causing bodily harm, although he did conclude the officer had made an error in judgement by not having his lights and siren on as he raced through the intersection.
Ramirez, who admitted to having great anger over the crash, said she had managed to forgive Brander for his role.
"I forgive him ... I cannot say who is at fault ... it just happened," she said.
News of the settlement came Monday as the family's lawsuit was about to start in an Edmonton courtroom. The suit was asking for $5 million in damages.
